scenes.heading: Working with agencies and white-label design work

sents.d: Working with agencies and white-label design work
Agency work trades some independence for steadier, higher-volume income.

Taking on white-label design work for agencies (where the agency, not you, is client-facing) can provide steadier volume than direct client work, since the agency handles sales and client management — you just need to deliver consistently on brief and on time.
Rates are typically lower per project than direct client work, since the agency needs their own margin, but the tradeoff is less time spent on sales, pitching, and client management overhead.
Clarifying upfront whether you can showcase agency work in your own portfolio matters — some agencies require confidentiality, which affects how useful that work is for your own marketing later.

take: White-label work trades rate for steady volume; clarify showcase rights.
